$comment: The concept layer. A concept is an idea a lab teaches (Instructions, Knowledge, Skills, MCP servers, ...) independent of which Copilot Studio harness implements it. Each concept lists the catalog features that teach it; a feature's own `harness` tag says which harnesses it applies to, so the same concept can map to a Standard harness feature, a Microsoft Copilot harness feature, and a Customer Conversation harness feature. `notApplicable` explains, per harness, why a concept has no equivalent there, so the wizard can say so instead of hiding the idea. Every catalog feature belongs to exactly one concept (validateConcepts enforces this). `order` is the teaching order the wizard lists concepts in. Do not name the Microsoft Copilot harness anything else, and use US English.

concepts.name: Choose a harness
concepts.summary: Decide which Copilot Studio harness fits the scenario, and how to move an existing agent.

concepts.name: Create an agent
concepts.summary: Make the agent object everything else hangs off.

concepts.name: Instructions
concepts.summary: Tell the agent who it is, what it covers, and how to behave.

concepts.name: Model and orchestration
concepts.summary: Choose the model and let the agent decide which tool or knowledge source to use.

concepts.name: Knowledge
concepts.summary: Ground answers in your documents, sites, and data.

concepts.name: Tools and connectors
concepts.summary: Let the agent take actions through connectors, custom connectors, and computer use.

concepts.name: Skills and prompt tools
concepts.summary: Reusable, structured behaviors. The Standard harness uses prompt tools; the Microsoft Copilot harness uses skills.

concepts.name: MCP servers
concepts.summary: Connect Model Context Protocol servers so the agent can use shared tools and resources.

concepts.name: Subagents and connected agents
concepts.summary: Delegate focused work to other agents, including agents in other products.

concepts.name: SDK and extensibility
concepts.summary: Author agents from code and embed them in your own apps.

notApplicable.customer-conversation: Not confirmed in Microsoft Learn: the Customer Conversation pages describe building agents on the Build tab and embedding web chat with a copied script, and none describe SDK or code-first authoring.

concepts.name: Memory
concepts.summary: Let the agent remember details across conversations.

notApplicable.standard: The Standard harness does not have memory; context lives in topics and variables.

concepts.name: Files and code execution
concepts.summary: Create and edit documents and run code in a sandbox.

notApplicable.standard: The Standard harness does not focus on creating or editing files.
notApplicable.customer-conversation: Learn's harness comparison lists working with files as not a focus of the Customer Conversation harness, and its pages describe no file creation or code execution.

concepts.name: Conversation design
concepts.summary: Control the conversation with topics, entities, variables, Adaptive Cards, and Power Fx.

notApplicable.microsoft-copilot: The Microsoft Copilot harness describes behavior in instructions instead of authoring topic flows. Hooks cover lifecycle moments.

concepts.name: Hooks
concepts.summary: Run logic automatically at set points in an agent's lifecycle.

notApplicable.standard: The Standard harness uses topics and system triggers for this.
notApplicable.customer-conversation: Not confirmed in Microsoft Learn: the Customer Conversation pages describe built-in events such as Conversation Start, End of Conversation, and On Error, not lifecycle hooks.

concepts.name: Triggers
concepts.summary: Start the agent from events rather than a person's message.

notApplicable.standard: Standard agents are triggered through topics and agent flows.
notApplicable.customer-conversation: Not confirmed in Microsoft Learn: the agent creation page mentions suggested triggers without detail, and no Customer Conversation page describes event-based or autonomous triggers, since customers start conversations over voice or chat.

concepts.name: Workflows and flows
concepts.summary: Run repeatable, predictable steps, with or without AI in the loop.

concepts.name: Enterprise systems and Microsoft 365
concepts.summary: Connect to systems of record such as ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, Epic, and Microsoft 365 data.

concepts.name: Testing and evaluation
concepts.summary: Prove the agent works and keeps working.

concepts.name: Monitor and analytics
concepts.summary: See how the agent performs in use.

concepts.name: Publish and channels
concepts.summary: Put the agent in front of people on Teams, the web, or voice.

concepts.name: Authentication and safety
concepts.summary: Control who can use the agent, what it may say, and which identity it runs as.

concepts.name: Governance and ALM
concepts.summary: Move agents between environments safely and keep an inventory under policy.

concepts.name: Credits and billing
concepts.summary: Understand what an agent costs to build, test, and run.
